thread:
Jonah: quick check — for the new private-cust rollout do we want per-tenant pipelines (agent-side split) or keep a multiplexed gateway and implement tenant-affinity routing? pros/cons pls.
Alex: per-tenant pipelines = nice isolation (retention, exports, egress billing) but much more ops and memory footprint on gateway/collector fleet.
Priya: can we get most isolation with logical isolation + quotas on a shared pipeline? routing + per-tenant exporters might be enough for many customers.
Sam: fwiw we saw a production case where shared pipeline + heavy tenant caused KV cache churn -> tail latency. that was spans-heavy (large traces) not metrics.
Mei: hybrid idea — keep metrics/health in shared pipeline, move spans to per-tenant pipelines when trace volume > threshold. cheaper for small tenants.
Jonah: console/UX question: if we do hybrid we need to surface "effective topology" in the UI so SREs know where a tenant's traces live for retention/exports. Otherwise support will be swamped.
Alex: agree. also we need rollout plan: start all private customers on multiplexed with per-tenant opt-in flag, then auto-migrate heavy tenants to per-tenant mode.
Priya: what about quotas? we should have token-bucket per-tenant at router layer before batching to avoid one tenant filling batch windows.
Sam: +1. code snippet we used in staging for routing policy (pseudo):
```
routing:
  mode: tenant_affinity
  default_exporter: shared-exporter
  per_tenant_threshold_bytes: 104857600 # 100MB/day
  overflow_action: isolate_to_tenant_pipeline
```
Mei: curious about retention enforcement: if a tenant is isolated to its own pipeline, do we push retention config to its exporter or enforce at storage gateway? Which is simpler for Private customers?
Alex: push config to exporter for private on-prem — customer can control S3/compat. For hosted/dedicated we enforce retention at storage gateway so we don't rely on per-tenant collector config drift.
Jonah: Ops question — memory pressure during peak: per-tenant pipelines -> more small exporter processes. multiplexed -> single big process with heavy KV cache. Which is easier to scale horizontally?
Sam: horizontal scaling is easier with per-tenant (shard by tenant) but requires smarter routing layer to place tenant shards. multiplexed is simpler to reason about but demonstrates noisy-neighbor.
Priya: UX tradeoff: can we show "recommended topology" in console (small icon) + button to request migration? then support/SE can approve.
Mei: + that. also need a telemetry metric for "migrations in progress" and one for "routing overflow count" to catch misconfig.
Alex: deploy-bot reported: "deploy-bot: canary deployed collector-splitter v2 to staging (routing + overflow_action) — tests running :rocket:"
Jonah: next steps: Priya to draft console mockups for migration flow, Sam + Alex to run a stress test with mixed small/large tenants to measure tail latency, Mei to enumerate retention enforcement options. I'll sync with infra next week on routing policy rollout.
Priya: noted, will post mocks by EOD Thursday.
Sam: I'll schedule the stress job and post results in this thread. timeline ~48h.
Mei: I'll write up retention options (config push vs storage enforcement) and list security implications.
Jonah: thanks everyone :thumbsup: — looping in @deploy-bot logs above for observability. We'll reconvene after the tests.
